name: Their Text, Not Ours
why_it_works: A customer's own words, shown as a real-looking message, borrow trust the brand cannot claim for itself. Starting from the thank-you and rewinding makes viewers curious how the problem got solved, and the viewer sees their own problem in the before.

hook.pattern: Open on the customer's thank-you message on screen with no voiceover, then rewind to how they got there.
examples: A customer sent us this. We asked to share it.
This text came in at 11pm last night.

variables.name: customer_quote
variables.description: The customer's real message, used with written permission, 6 words or fewer
variables.example: You saved my road trip. Thank you.

variables.name: customer_first_name
variables.description: Customer first name, with permission, or a stand-in like 'One driver'

variables.name: problem
variables.description: The problem they arrived with, in plain words, spoken, 9 words or fewer
variables.example: a dashboard full of warning lights before a trip

variables.name: what_we_did
variables.description: The specific fix or service, plainly described, starting with a past-tense verb, 11 words or fewer
variables.example: found a loose sensor wire instead of replacing the whole unit

variables.name: after_state
variables.description: Where they are now, in their terms, 6 words or fewer

variables.name: offer
variables.description: What the viewer gets for acting, a short phrase starting with a capital letter, 6 words or fewer

variables.name: early_signs
variables.description: Three early warning signs of the same problem, as a short list
variables.example: a new noise, a warning light, or a smell when braking

variables.name: save_tip
variables.description: One practical tip that saves the viewer time or money before they book, a full sentence
variables.example: Snap a photo of the dashboard lights before you call; it saves a diagnosis step.

beats.purpose: hook: the customer's real text, verbatim

visual.prompt: Client-supplied screenshot of the real customer text message reading {{customer_quote}}, shared with written permission, phone number and surname blurred

beats.purpose: who they were and what was wrong

visual.prompt: Client-supplied photo of the real customer or their car, phone or paperwork at {{brand}}, used with written consent; no face if they asked for none
Close-up of a {{brand}} team member's hands doing {{what_we_did}}, clean bright workspace, shallow depth of field, vertical 9:16

beats.purpose: the turn: where they are now

visual.prompt: Client-supplied photo of the real customer after the fix, or the result itself, at {{brand}}, used with written consent

slides.headline: "{{customer_quote}}"
slides.body: A real message we got from {{customer_first_name}}.
slides.visual_prompt: Client-supplied screenshot of the real customer message, {{brand}} colors framing it

slides.headline: How it started
slides.visual_prompt: Close-up of the problem itself at {{brand}}, no people, natural window light

slides.headline: What we did
slides.visual_prompt: Close-up of hands doing the work at {{brand}}, bright clean workspace

slides.headline: Where they are now
slides.visual_prompt: Clean result shot at {{brand}}, warm daylight, no customer face

slides.headline: Catch it early: three signs
slides.body: Watch for {{early_signs}}. Save this for later.
slides.visual_prompt: Simple checklist graphic with three tick boxes in {{brand}} colors, clean flat layout

slides.headline: Before you book: one tip
slides.visual_prompt: Flat-lay of a phone, notepad and pen on a clean desk at {{brand}}, soft daylight

slides.headline: Got the same problem?
slides.visual_prompt: Clean {{brand}} logo card with the offer in large type

craft.technique: Start at the ending, then rewind
craft.notes: The first frame is the payoff in the customer's own words, silent so people read it, from a real screenshot. Then rewind to the problem. The middle beat shows the work, not the staff smiling. Keep the after concrete: a number, a distance, a date. Every customer image is client-supplied, never generated.

do_not: Write a fake review or fake text message
Show a customer's face or name without written permission
Turn the middle beat into a sales pitch
Generate a face or photo to stand in for the real customer
compliance: Customer screenshots and photos are client-supplied real_photo only, with written consent; never a generated customer
Only use real customer messages with written permission; keep the permission on file
Dental, chiropractic and med spa: no patient names, faces or health details without a signed HIPAA-compliant authorization, and no promise that the viewer will get the same result
Med spa: any before/after mention needs 'Results vary' on screen
Insurance and real estate: no claim of guaranteed savings, coverage or sale price; include license number where your state requires it
